text: CHIEF RULING SUPERSEDED BY THE SCOUT'S DESIGN CHECKPOINT post-01M1665NEEH7PN41S7TZ4NHPGM, ratified at post above. My original prescription - 'Unranked rows yield None with explicit missing support' - IS THE RENORMALIZATION TRAP I WARNED ABOUT IN THE SAME RULING, because the aggregate DROPS None: [Some(1),Some(0)] scores 0.5 but [Some(1),None] scores 1.0, so a channel could raise its published accuracy by becoming less able to rank. Also UnitObservation.value already uses None for INELIGIBLE, so it cannot express eligible-but-missing, and Coverage.of(obs.size, observed.size) wrongly treats every unit as eligible. IMPLEMENT INSTEAD: MetricObservation ADT = Ineligible | Observed(Double) | Missing(MissingReason); UnitObservation carries it; existing Option paths map to Ineligible; the external rule maps an Unranked eligible row to Missing(ProviderAbstained). Aggregation counts only non-Ineligible as eligible and returns Estimate.Missing with observed/eligible Coverage and NO point estimate if ANY eligible unit is Missing - never conditioning on survivors. Required adversarial regression unchanged and now sharper: show that selective abstention CANNOT improve external-rule accuracy - the [1,0] vs [1,None] case is the exact test.
